assumptions: Because the input provided no structured SpecJson state names, the twelve required states are named descriptively from the natural-language dispatch cases.

The model is encoded as a guard-driven condition-classification FSM using forced guarded transitions from any current state, because the NL says states are selected by logical transition conditions over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC rather than by named external events.
The NL gives the full-battery threshold 0.95 but does not give the lower SoC value for battery discharge suitability; this initial candidate uses SoC >= 0.2 as a provisional suitability threshold.

Pgmax is modeled as LNG capacity, Pd1max as DG1 capacity, and eng3_Pmax as DG2 capacity because the NL names LNG, DG1/DG2 priority and mentions engine capacity bounds such as eng3_Pmax but does not provide a complete variable dictionary.
PV and WEC renewable sources are treated as read-only contributions Ppv and Pw rather than cut-in/cut-out commanded units; generator cut commands are modeled for LNG, DG1, and DG2.

Load cut-in/cut-out commands are represented as demand-present service commands: cutin_load is asserted when PL > 0 and cutout_load when PL == 0. The NL does not define individual load-shedding branches.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: When PL = 0, RES production is sent to battery charging according to SoC thresholds.
When PL = 0, RES production is sent to spare power according to SoC thresholds.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, the EMS serves all ship demand from RES and charges batteries while SoC is below 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw covers PL, residual renewable power is spare once SoC is at least 0.95.
When Ppv + Pw is below PL, dispatch follows priority: RES first, batteries when SoC is suitable.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including Pgmax/5 in an LNG-covered case.
When RES is below PL, LNG is used before diesel units.
Low-SoC branches add explicit charging margins, including Pd1max/10 in later diesel-generator cases.

decisions.rationale: Pbat_Pmax is an externally supplied battery power capacity/input bound used to classify dispatch states. The NL says the FSM reads load, renewable, SoC, and capacity-bound inputs; it does not provide any internal update law for battery maximum power. Adding a write or self-assignment would invent plant dynamics or a meaningless warning-silencer.

The BatteryDischargeOnly classification guard from ZeroLoadCharge depends only on external operating-condition inputs: PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, and Pbat_Pmax. The warning is expected for a condition-classification FSM whose inputs are read from the environment.

The LNGCoverChargeMargin guard from ZeroLoadCharge uses external demand/resource/capacity inputs. No NL-grounded internal write exists for PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, Pgmax, or Pbat_Pmax, so editing the DSL would either remove required classification logic or invent dynamics.
The BatteryDischargeOnly classification guard from ZeroLoadSpare is intentionally governed by external input values. Preserving the NL-required guard is safer than adding artificial writes.

The LNGCoverChargeMargin guard from ZeroLoadSpare is part of the required dispatch classification over external demand, RES, SoC, and capacity values. No safe NL-grounded repair exists for the warning.

The BatteryDischargeOnly guard from RESCoverCharge reads only external operating-condition variables, which is consistent with the NL requirement that states are selected by logical conditions over demand, generation, capacity, and SoC.
The LNGCoverChargeMargin guard from RESCoverCharge must remain a guard over external inputs and capacity bounds. Adding dummy assignments would violate the forbidden-edits guidance.
The BatteryDischargeOnly guard from RESCoverSpare is correctly driven by external inputs. There is no NL evidence for internally changing PL, Ppv, Pw, SoC, or Pbat_Pmax inside the EMS.

The LNGCoverChargeMargin guard from RESCoverSpare reflects required dispatch selection logic over external condition variables. A repair would either delete grounded behavior or invent update semantics.

The self-classification to BatteryDischargeOnly remains valid when the same external demand/resource/SoC/capacity condition persists. The guard variables are intentionally external inputs, not internal state variables.

The current DSL’s required twelve states, cut-in/cut-out actions, output power requests, charging/discharging outputs, spare power, and guarded classification transitions are NL-grounded and should be preserved.

No safe smallest edit exists: adding assignments would be meaningless or would invent plant/environment dynamics; replacing guards with constants would break dispatch classification; deleting Pbat_Pmax would remove the battery discharge capacity condition.
